decisions.reason: The weir dimensioning web tool is cheap to maintain, ties directly into the firm's core flood-control offer and the new flap weir products D and F, and supports planner relationships, so withdrawing it makes no sense.

Product A, its automation counterpart, has already been dropped, but management has invested in this fouling detection system and showcased it publicly as part of its energy-efficiency direction, so it will attribute weak uptake to market-development delays and keep it for now.

The spring-controlled flap weir was only launched in 2024, sits close to the firm's established hydraulic steel-structure business, and fits long municipal project cycles, so it is far too early to judge its results.

The energy management system for water facilities is central to the announced direction of digital networking, efficiency and energy recovery, so management is strongly committed to it despite any slow start.
The overflow flap gate line has several models and its own website page, reflecting substantial investment and visible commitment in a core business area, making withdrawal very unlikely.
